test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 09 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The capacity of a cuboid tank of water is 70,000 litres. Find the breadth of the tank, if its length and depth are 4 m and 10 m, respectively.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume in m³ = 70,000 ÷ 1,000 = 70 m³

Breadth = Volume ÷ (Length × Depth)

Breadth = 70 ÷ (4 × 10) = 70 ÷ 40 = 1.75 m

**∴ The correct answer is 1.75 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Capacity of tank = 70,000 litres

Length (l) = 4 m

Depth (h) = 10 m

**Formula Used:**

1 m³ = 1,000 litres

Volume of a cuboid = Length × Breadth × Height

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9e0ad7b8790843e6cd8965140419dcea71c7b81e0783428c8ef18342b26eecc9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume in cubic meters = 70,000 ÷ 1,000 = 70 m³

⇒ Volume = l × b × h

⇒ 70 = 4 × b × 10

⇒ 70 = 40 × b

⇒ b = 70 ÷ 40

⇒ b = 1.75 m

**∴ The correct answer is 1.75 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cuboid

The space occupied by a three-dimensional rectangular object is given by Volume = Length × Breadth × Height.

Unit Conversions

1 m³ = 1,000 litres and 1 litre = 1,000 cm³.

Surface Area of Cuboid

Total Surface Area = 2(lb + bh + hl) and Lateral Surface Area = 2h(l + b).</p
